subject: Q2 usage readout & proposed extension/addendum
messages:
From: Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Rivera <alex@orchid.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 12 Jul 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Q2 usage readout & proposed extension/addendum

Hi Alex —

Thanks again for taking the time last week. Attached is the Q2 usage report we promised; highlights below so you can skim quickly: 

- Token mix: 62% short-form generation (<=64 tokens), 28% chat/dialog, 10% embeddings/rerank.
- Monthly run-rate: ~3.9M tokens/day average in June; projected to 4.6M/day with the new feature rollout.
- Latency: p95 unchanged at 180ms on your dedicated pool after prefetch tuning.
- Cost efficiency: 11% lower per-token after applying the prefix cache suggestions we shipped.

Given the trajectory and the feature rollout you mentioned, our recommendation is a modest headroom increase (50% committed cushion) plus a 12-month addendum that preserves current unit pricing and adds a burst lane for peak traffic. I attached a draft addendum (proposed-addendum.docx) that:

1) Increases committed monthly tokens by 50% for the next 12 months
2) Adds a 7-day burst credit pool for product launches (one-time drawdown option)
3) Preserves existing SLA credits and includes a 30-day review clause for burst usage

If this looks reasonable, happy to route the addendum to your procurement team and set up a short call to walk through assumptions.

Next steps I propose:
- You confirm interest in the headroom + addendum by EOD Wed, Jul 14
- We schedule a 30-min ops walk-through (Ben + Monica onsite) to review the burst mechanics
- We prepare a DocuSign-ready version for Procurement if you give the green light

Thanks —

Tessa Morgan
Account Lead, Strategic Customers
Redwood Inference
(t) 415-555-0123

Attachments: q2-usage-report.pdf, proposed-addendum.docx
From: Alex Rivera <alex@orchid.ai>
To: Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.ai>
Cc: Procurement <procurement@orchid.ai>
Date: Mon, 12 Jul 2027 11:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Q2 usage readout & proposed extension/addendum

Tessa —

Appreciate the concise breakdown and the proactive plan. A couple quick clarifying items before I loop procurement: 

- The 50% headroom — is that applied to our current committed tier (monthly tokens) or to the run-rate estimate? We want to make sure it’s on the committed bucket so our forecasting stays simple.
- For the burst lane: can you confirm how 'drawdown' is tracked? Do we get real-time visibility in the console or only via monthly reporting?

Procurement here (cc’d) will need the final addendum with a line-item for billing cadence and an example month where burst is used so they understand invoicing.

Also, minor ask — can you include an estimate of expected cost delta assuming we use 30% of the burst credits in Q4 (ballpark numbers are fine).

We’re inclined to proceed but want the operational clarity before signing.

—Alex
Product Lead, Orchid Analytics
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
To: Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 12 Jul 2027 12:10:00 -07:00
Subject: Fwd: Q2 usage readout & proposed extension/addendum

Tessa / Monica —

Looping in to propose how we answer Alex above: 

1) Headroom: we should frame it explicitly as an increase to the committed monthly tokens (so Orchid gets predictable capacity and accounting stays simple). Say: 'committed monthly tokens will be increased by 50% relative to the currently contracted monthly commitment.'

2) Burst drawdown visibility: we can offer console visibility — real-time burst usage dashboard + alerting — and include a one-page ops runbook as an appendix. That should satisfy Procurement and Ops.

3) Cost delta: rough math: if their current blended unit is $0.0008/token, and burst billing rate is 1.35x (applied only when burst is consumed), then using 30% of a 50% headroom over one month moves invoice by approx $9k–$12k depending on token mix. We should include both conservative and aggressive estimates in the addendum.

I'll draft the two-paragraph explainer and the example invoice; Monica can add the runbook snippet. Tessa — want me to attach my draft and send direct to Procurement, or do you want to consolidate first?

—Ben
Senior AE, Redwood Inference
From: Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.ai>

Date: Tue, 13 Jul 2027 15:07:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Q2 usage readout & proposed extension/addendum

Alex / Procurement —

Thanks for the quick reply. Attached is a revised addendum and a 1-page operations appendix (we included the console screenshots) — both documents are DocuSign-ready: https://www.docusign.com/link/abc123-addendum

Answers inline: 
- Headroom: confirmed — 50% increase applies to the committed monthly tokens line item. Example: contracted = 3M tokens/month -> new committed = 4.5M tokens/month.
- Burst drawdown: real-time visibility in Console + daily usage emails; billing shows burst consumption as a separate line item flagged 'consumed-burst-credit'. Example invoice attached for a sample month (30% burst consumption scenario) showing the ~$10k delta Ben estimated.

Next steps: 
1) Procurement: if you confirm the billing cadence (monthly invoice) and acceptance of the example invoice, we’ll send the DocuSign package for signatures.
2) Ops call: Ben and Monica are available Wed 14 or Thu 15 (30 minutes). Please pick a slot and we’ll lock it in.

If Procurement wants a legal redline first, Monica will coordinate with Legal — otherwise we can proceed to signatures.

Best —
